title: Chapter 10 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of Advanced Patterns & Internals!

questions.question: In the App Router, what directive marks a component as a Client Component?
questions.explanation: Add `'use client'` at the top of the file to make it a Client Component.

questions.question: Which of the following can a Server Component do?
questions.explanation: Server Components run on the server and can directly query databases, read files, etc. They cannot use state or effects.

questions.question: A Client Component can directly import and render a Server Component.
questions.explanation: A Client Component cannot import a Server Component. However, it can receive one as children from a parent Server Component.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `loading.js` file in the App Router?
options: To define a global loading state for the entire app
To automatically wrap the corresponding page in a Suspense boundary, showing a fallback while the page content loads
To configure the loading spinner animation
To preload data for a page
questions.explanation: `loading.js` acts as a Suspense fallback for the page, enabling streaming of the page shell before data arrives.

questions.question: To stream a specific component independently, you manually wrap it in a `<______>` tag with a fallback prop.
questions.explanation: `<Suspense fallback={...}>` allows you to define a loading state for a specific part of the page, enabling granular streaming.

questions.question: What is a key benefit of streaming SSR?
options: It reduces the total server processing time
Users see the page shell and static content immediately, without waiting for slow data fetches
It eliminates the need for a loading state
questions.explanation: Streaming sends the HTML in chunks, so the browser can start rendering the page while waiting for slower components.

questions.question: How are parallel routes defined in the file system?
options: By creating files with a `parallel.` prefix
By creating folders with an `@` prefix
questions.explanation: Folders named `@something` in a segment act as parallel route slots, and the layout receives a prop with that name.

questions.question: An error in one parallel route slot causes all slots to show the error.
questions.explanation: Each slot is an independent tree. An error in one slot triggers only that slot's error boundary, leaving other slots intact.

questions.question: Which folder convention intercepts navigation to a route one level up from the current segment?
questions.explanation: `(..)` goes up one level. So from `app/feed/`, `(..)photo` would intercept `app/photo`.

questions.question: What is the primary use case for intercepting routes?
options: To implement modal/overlay patterns that update the URL without losing the underlying page context
To redirect users based on authentication
questions.explanation: Intercepting routes show a different UI (like a modal) when navigating from a specific context, while still keeping the URL shareable.

questions.question: When a user refreshes the browser on an intercepted route URL, Next.js renders the ______ page because there is no navigation source to intercept.
questions.explanation: Hard navigations (refresh, direct URL) always render the real page file, not the intercepted one.

questions.question: In the photo gallery example, which file renders the modal when navigating from the gallery to a photo?
questions.explanation: The intercepted route is placed inside the gallery segment using `(..)photo` to catch navigation to `/photo/[id]`.

questions.question: You can use `useState` inside a Server Component if you wrap it in a `<Suspense>` boundary.
questions.explanation: Server Components cannot contain hooks that manage state or effects. Interactivity must be in a Client Component.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid way to pass a Server Component into a Client Component?
options: Import it in the Client Component file
Render it as a children prop from a parent Server Component
Use the `server` attribute on the component
questions.explanation: The parent Server Component can render the Client Component and place the Server Component inside it via `children`, keeping the boundary intact.

questions.question: What happens when a page wrapped by a `loading.js` finishes fetching its data during streaming?
options: The server sends the resolved HTML chunk and React replaces the fallback in the DOM
The user is redirected to the new page
questions.explanation: React on the client listens for streamed updates and seamlessly swaps the fallback with the actual content.

questions.question: What is the advantage of combining parallel routes with intercepting routes?
options: You can have a modal (intercepted route) inside a slot that renders alongside other independent page sections
questions.explanation: Parallel routes and intercepting routes are independent but complementary. For example, a sidebar slot can exist alongside an intercepted modal route.

questions.question: Streaming requires a Vercel deployment to work.
questions.explanation: Streaming uses standard HTTP and React's `renderToReadableStream`. It works on any Node.js server that supports streaming responses.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid parallel route slot pattern?
questions.explanation: Slot names cannot contain path‑like segments or parentheses that clash with route grouping/intercepting conventions. They should be simple identifiers.
